newsitem.title: INDIA: India's I-Sec sees rally in gilt prices next week.
newsitem.headline: India's I-Sec sees rally in gilt prices next week.

text.p: ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-Sec) said it expected securities prices to rally next week following a cut in banks' cash reserve requirement.
The Reserve Bank is reducing the cash reserve requirement by half percentage point to 10 percent on Saturday, releasing over 20 billion rupees into the banking system.

"The next reserve cut is likely to initiate a strong rally in gilts since almost the entire amount released would be available for deployment in assets," Aashish Pitale of I-Sec debt research said in a debt market update.

The (previous) early January reserve cut failed to push up prices of government bonds primarily because call rates were ruling above 11 percent and a large portion of the funds made available through reserve reduction were utilised in repaying the export refinance availed by banks, the report said.
"Gains recorded by gilt-edged securities in the last fortnight of 1996 have almost entirely eroded in the first couple of weeks of the new year," it said.
Prices fell across the board by about 30 paise to 40 paise.
It said the drop in prices was more prominent in the medium and short-dated securities with long bonds holding ground, thanks to the strong demand from provident funds.
